transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I understand the inpatient team has submitted an emergency non-formulary approval request for Lunacavir for a patient who is medically stable and expected to be discharged later this week. Before I can make a final decision and sign off on the medication plan, I'd like to walk through our routine review process. We need to check in with infectious disease, utilization review, and outpatient pharmacy to make sure we have a clear picture on how this medication will be obtained and monitored, especially since Lunacavir isn't stocked on our formulary. Can we start by hearing from each of those areas?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share important clinical information. I received the susceptibility report this morning, and the patient's isolate is resistant to the two formulary alternatives. Infectious-disease guidance supports Lunacavir 400 mg twice daily for exactly 7 days. However, this susceptibility result has not yet been added to the medication request that was submitted.

transcript.text: I have critical information from the outpatient pharmacy side. Because the patient takes tacrolimus, outpatient pharmacy requires a tacrolimus trough before the first Lunacavir dose and a second trough on day 4.
